mt: 'INTERNATIONAL DADA ARCHIVE' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE ARCHIVE AT ITS GRAIN FROM ITS OWN PAGE; A 1978 CONFERENCE AND A WORLD RANK ADDED; THE BOOKS BY AUTHOR, WITH THEIR DOUBLE NAMES, NOT CARRIED
d: THE ARCHIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The International Dada Archive is a premier scholarly research center for the historic Dada movement, housed at the University of Iowa Libraries in Iowa City, Iowa.' Overview and history (founded 1979 'following a 1978 international Dada conference'; location; scope as 'One of the world's largest repositories'); collection and resources (the Online Bibliography of roughly 60,000 titles, the Digital Dada Library, formats, Dada/Surrealism); an offer to guide the user. Four cards: the University of Iowa Libraries, People’s Graphic Design Archive, The Gazette, International Times.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the archive, the Overview gives its founding, where its holdings sit, its catalog and digital library, its journal, and offers to point the user to an artist or periodical.
findings: THE ARCHIVE AT ITS GRAIN. The home page: 'Founded in 1979, the International Dada Archive is a scholarly resource for the study of the historic Dada movement.' and 'a catalog containing approximately 60,000 titles'. The composition: 'roughly 60,000 titles', and the location 'primarily split between the Main Library and the Art Library, with rare materials in Special Collections', which the page states as 'most of its holdings are in either the Main Library or the Art Library' with the Digital Dada Library's originals 'housed in the Special Collections Department'.

TWO ADDITIONS AND A ROLE SHIFTED. 'following a 1978 international Dada conference hosted at the university' and 'One of the world's largest repositories' are on no saved page. 'Co-publisher of the peer-reviewed scholarly journal Dada/Surrealism': the page makes the Archive its sole publisher, 'sponsored by the Association for the Study of Dada and Surrealism and published by the International Dada Archive, University of Iowa Libraries.'

THE BOOKS BY AUTHOR NOT CARRIED. The census reads the Digital Dada Library's author list as holding a pen name and a civil name side by side ('SALOMO FRIEDLAENDER (MYNONA)', 'Iliazd (Ilia Zdanevich)') and one book under both: 'JULIUS KREKEL (CLÉMENT PANSAERS): ZIEK; EENE MOEDER; HERTETOLKEN' and, under 'CLÉMENT PANSAERS', the same 'ZIEK; EENE MOEDER; HERTETOLKEN'. The composition offers help with 'An individual artist or writer you want to research' and gives no account of how the list files a writer.

THE TERMS AND THE CURATOR NOT CARRIED. 'These documents are provided for research purposes only.'; 'Your library should treat the International Dada Archive as a "lender of last resort."'; 'Timothy Shipe, Curator'. The composition names the Libraries and neither the curator nor the terms; its 'scanned images' agrees with 'These are page-image files only, not searchable full-text files.'
analysis: Faithful to the archive's own page on founding, holdings and count, with a conference, a world rank and a co-publisher on no saved page. The author list the census reads it for, where one book stands under a pen name and a civil name, is absent.
per_note: The University of Iowa Libraries named; the curator not named; the archive's own page carded first.

evidence.record_quote: Founded in 1979, the International Dada Archive is a scholarly resource for the study of the historic Dada movement. The Archive has compiled a comprehensive collection of documentation and scholarship relating to Dada.

atoms.reference: Works by and about the dadaists (books, articles, microfilmed manuscript collections, video and sound recordings, online resources); the International Online Bibliography of Dada, about 60,000 titles; the Digital Dada Library of page scans of periodicals, books, catalogs and broadsides.

evidence.record_quote: The collection of the International Dada Archive is made up of works by and about the dadaists including books, articles, microfilmed manuscript collections, videorecordings, sound recordings, and online resources.
Primary access to the entire collection is through the International Online Bibliography of Dada, a catalog containing approximately 60,000 titles.

These books, pamphlets, and periodicals are housed in the Special Collections Department of the University of Iowa Libraries and include many of the major periodicals of the Dada movement from Zurich, Berlin, Paris, and elsewhere, as well as books, exhibition catalogs, and broadsides by participants in the Dada movement.

The Archive has also microfilmed a number of public and private manuscript collections containing material on the Dada movement and on individual dadaists. Detailed finding aids exist for each of these microfilmed collections.

atoms.reference: Scans for research purposes only; copyrighted matter omitted from scanned reprints; a lender of last resort, unpublished manuscripts not normally loaned.

evidence.record_quote: These documents are provided for research purposes only.

In a few cases, for the sake of completeness, we have included reprints of issues for which we do not own originals; in those cases, we have omitted any copyrighted materials such as new prefaces and critical annotations.
Your library should treat the International Dada Archive as a "lender of last resort."
Unpublished manuscript material cannot normally be loaned.
